newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends weaker pressured by fund sales.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends weaker pressured by fund sales.

text.p: Fund sellers kept robusta coffee futures under pressure during Wednesday's session as the London market broadly mirrored the choppy trade seen in New York, market sources said.

London's benchmark July contract spent the day in a $74 range but was in negative territory all the time, closing down $125 on the day at $1,695 and thus near its $1,700 open. Its intraday low was $1,666.
Traders said more liquidation had poured into the market on the back of New York's steep losses on Tuesday and London was still cautious of volatility in arabicas.
Fund players liquidated positions as sell stops were triggered but bargain hunters were quick to move in and snap up bargains at the lows, they said.
"Once again people came in and picked a few bottoms here and there and it rallied $70 as quickly as it came off -- the usual coffee story," said one.
September closed $115 lower at $1,735 and volume amounted to 9,949 lots.
Prices showed little reaction to news that Colombia produced 836,000 60-kg bags of coffee in May, up a surprising 12.21 percent over the 745,000 bags produced during the same month last year.
Sources at the National Coffee Growers' Federation said production from October 1996 through May 1997 totalled just 7.29 million bags, however, down from 9.9 million in October 1995 through May 1997.
